statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A DCCP sender SHOULD send every packet as unfragmentable, as described above, with the following exceptions.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On IPv4 connections whose applications have requested fragmentation, the sender SHOULD send packets with the DF bit not set.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On IPv6 connections whose applications have requested fragmentation, the sender SHOULD use fragmentation extension headers to fragment packets larger than PMTU into suitably-sized chunks.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Thus, DCCP-Request and DCCP-Response packets SHOULD be sent as fragmentable.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In addition, DCCP-Reset packets SHOULD be sent as fragmentable, although typically these would be small enough to not be a problem.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For IPv4 connections, these packets SHOULD be sent with the DF bit not set; for IPv6 connections, they SHOULD be preemptively fragmented to a size not larger than the relevant interface MTU.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the DCCP implementation has decreased the PMTU, the sending application has not requested fragmentation, and the sending application attempts to send a packet larger than the new MPS, the API MUST refuse to send the packet and return an appropriate error to the application.
statements.pre_cond: dccp.pmtu_decreased = true & application.fragmentation_requested = false & packet.size > connection.mps

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: It MAY send these packets as fragmentable, or it MAY discard these packets; it MUST NOT send them as unfragmentable.
statements.pre_cond: dccp.pmtu_decreased = true & packet.buffered = true & packet.size > connection.new_mps & packet.size <= connection.old_mps
